items.title: Receipt is a closed object with six required members
items.statement: A valid receipt is an object, rejects undeclared top-level properties, and requires schema_id, packet_id, received_packet, files, finding_matrix, and negative_constraints.

items.title: Receipt schema discriminator is exact
items.statement: schema_id must equal pm.web_capability_source_packet_receipt.v1.

items.title: Packet identifiers are nonempty strings
items.statement: packet_id and received_packet are required to be strings of at least one character.

items.title: Receipt inventories at least four packet files
items.statement: files is an array with at least four entries, and each entry is validated through the PacketFile definition.

items.title: Finding matrix is closed and has six required fields
items.statement: finding_matrix rejects undeclared properties and requires schema_id, generated_at_utc, source_repo, supersedes, finding_ids, and finding_priorities.

items.title: Finding matrix schema discriminator is exact
items.statement: The embedded finding matrix must identify itself as pm.web_capability_findings_matrix.v3.

items.title: Finding identifiers have a minimum cardinality and uniqueness oracle
items.statement: finding_ids must contain at least nineteen unique, nonempty strings.

items.title: Priority values are constrained
items.statement: Every property value present in finding_priorities must be one of P0, P1, P2, or P3.

items.title: At least one negative constraint is mandatory
items.statement: negative_constraints must be an array containing at least one nonempty string.

items.title: Packet-file records are closed and structurally complete
items.statement: Each PacketFile rejects undeclared properties and requires artifact_name, artifact_role, sha256, and byte_size.

items.title: Artifact roles use a four-value vocabulary
items.statement: artifact_role is restricted to review_addendum, findings_matrix, goal_prompt, or source_packet_archive.

items.title: Artifact digest and size have syntactic oracles
items.statement: sha256 must be exactly sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal characters and byte_size must be an integer of at least one.

items.title: Four artifact roles are not guaranteed to be represented
items.statement: The schema requires only four PacketFile entries and validates each role independently; it does not require exactly one file for each of the four role values. Four duplicate-role entries can satisfy the receipt while a required semantic artifact role is absent.
items.impact: A structurally valid receipt can describe an incomplete or role-duplicated source packet.
items.builder_discretion: A consumer must decide whether to require exact role coverage, reject duplicate roles, and permit extra files.

items.title: Artifact identity is not unique or related to role
items.statement: artifact_name is only a nonempty string, and the files array has no uniqueness or cross-field rule. Duplicate names, duplicate records, or conflicting name-to-role mappings remain schema-valid.
items.impact: Consumers may select different artifacts or silently overwrite entries.
items.builder_discretion: Consumers must invent artifact naming, duplicate handling, and name-to-role identity rules.

items.title: Packet identity fields have no defined syntax or relationship
items.statement: packet_id and received_packet are independently constrained only as nonempty strings. The schema does not say whether received_packet is a path, URI, filename, digest, or logical ID, nor bind either value to the file inventory.
items.impact: A valid receipt can identify a different packet than the listed artifacts, and consumers cannot interpret the locator consistently.
items.builder_discretion: Implementers must choose identifier formats, normalization, and cross-field binding rules.

items.title: Finding priorities are not total or keyed to finding identifiers
items.statement: finding_priorities may be an empty object or contain arbitrary keys because only property values are constrained. No contract requires one priority for each finding_id or forbids priorities for unknown IDs.
items.impact: A matrix can carry nineteen findings while omitting every priority, or can prioritize unrelated identifiers.
items.builder_discretion: A consumer must decide whether priority coverage is total, partial, or defaulted and how extraneous keys are treated.

items.title: Timestamp and repository provenance are weakly typed
items.statement: generated_at_utc and source_repo accept any nonempty strings. UTC/date-time syntax, repository URI or canonical identity, and revision binding are not validated.
items.impact: Ordering, freshness, repository attribution, and reproducible source selection cannot be trusted from schema validity.
items.builder_discretion: Producers and consumers must choose timestamp, repository locator, and revision conventions.

items.title: Supersession lineage permits empty, duplicate, and untyped references
items.statement: supersedes is only an array of nonempty strings; it has no minimum cardinality, uniqueness rule, identifier format, or existence check.
items.impact: Lineage may be ambiguous, duplicated, dangling, or absent while the matrix remains valid.
items.builder_discretion: Implementers must define reference identity, resolution, cycle handling, and whether empty lineage is allowed.

items.title: Negative constraints are opaque and non-unique
items.statement: The contract requires at least one nonempty negative-constraint string but defines no identifiers, scope, structured semantics, uniqueness, or enforcement oracle.
items.impact: Producers can satisfy the schema with duplicate or semantically empty prose, and consumers may interpret constraints differently.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must decide parsing, deduplication, scope, conflict handling, and enforcement behavior.

items.title: Artifact integrity fields are not bound to artifact bytes
items.statement: The schema validates only digest syntax and positive size. It cannot establish that the named artifact exists, that its bytes hash to sha256, or that byte_size matches those bytes.
items.impact: A schema-valid receipt can make false integrity and size claims, so ingestion without executable verification is unsafe.
items.builder_discretion: A consumer must define byte acquisition, hashing, size checking, mismatch handling, and retry or quarantine behavior.

items.title: Receipt collections and strings are unbounded
items.statement: The contract supplies lower bounds but no maximum lengths or cardinalities for identifiers, files, supersedes, finding_ids, finding_priorities, negative constraints, or artifact names.
items.impact: An otherwise valid receipt can require excessive memory, CPU, storage, or downstream work.
items.builder_discretion: Implementers must choose payload, collection, and string limits and define limit-exceeded behavior.

items.title: Receipt authenticity and authority are absent
items.statement: The exhaustive top-level required-member list contains no producer identity, signer, signature, trust domain, authority grant, or verification metadata.
items.impact: Consumers cannot distinguish an authorized receipt from a forged or substituted one using this contract.
items.builder_discretion: The trust model, authorized producer set, signing mechanism, and rejection policy are entirely external.

items.title: Receipt and finding-matrix version compatibility is undeclared
items.statement: The receipt schema is version v1 while the embedded matrix discriminator is v3, but no compatibility, downgrade, upgrade, or migration behavior is expressed.
items.impact: Implementers cannot determine which future or prior matrix versions a receipt version may accept or how stored receipts evolve.
items.builder_discretion: Version negotiation and migration policy must be invented outside this schema.

items.title: Ownership, consumers, and propagation authority are unspecified
items.statement: The closed receipt shape names packet content but no owner, intended consumer, custodian, approver, retention owner, or authority governing how findings and constraints propagate.
items.impact: Multiple conforming implementations can route, retain, approve, and propagate the same receipt differently.
items.builder_discretion: Ownership assignments, consumer eligibility, lifecycle custody, and propagation rules remain external decisions.

items.title: Artifact names lack path and locator safety constraints
items.statement: artifact_name accepts any nonempty string, without basename-only, normalization, relative-path, traversal, URI-scheme, or character restrictions.
items.impact: A consumer that treats artifact_name as a filesystem or network locator could traverse directories or access unintended resources.
items.builder_discretion: Consumers must define whether names are opaque labels or locators and apply canonicalization and containment checks.

items.title: Failure states and recovery transitions are unspecified
items.statement: The receipt is a static object with no status, validation outcome, partial-ingestion state, quarantine state, retry counter, error detail, or transition contract for missing, corrupt, or rejected artifacts.
items.impact: Consumers can diverge on whether invalid or partially available packets are rejected, retried, quarantined, or accepted with warnings.
items.builder_discretion: Implementers must define the state machine, atomicity boundary, recovery actions, idempotency, and observability signals.

items.title: GUI behavior is not part of this receipt schema
items.statement: The source defines a JSON object contract for a source-packet receipt and contains no user-interface model or presentation behavior; gui_truth is therefore not applicable within this document window.

dimension_assessments.summary: The schema's validation behavior is explicit for object closure, required members, lower bounds, enumerations, uniqueness of finding IDs, and primitive constraints.
The receipt can identify a packet, inventory artifacts, embed a finding summary and priorities, and carry negative constraints, subject to semantic integrity gaps.
The JSON input shape is defined, but packet locators, artifact-byte binding, and output or processing outcomes are not.
Structural contracts are strong at each object boundary, while cross-field role coverage, identity, referential integrity, and semantic enforcement remain under-specified.
No lifecycle state or transition model exists for receipt creation, validation, acceptance, rejection, partial ingestion, quarantine, or recovery.
The contract has no producer authorization, signer, approver, or trust-domain binding.
No operational, data, retention, or recovery owner is identified in the closed receipt shape.
Intended consumers, their eligibility, and their obligations after validation are not specified.
This window is a JSON receipt schema and exposes no GUI state, layout, interaction, or presentation contract.
Digest and size syntax exist, but mismatch detection, atomic rejection, error reporting, retries, quarantine, rollback, and partial-packet recovery are unspecified.
Authenticity is absent and freeform artifact names can become unsafe locators; no confidentiality, redaction, or sensitive-field policy appears.
Finding priority keys are not bound to finding IDs, supersession references are weak, and no rule governs downstream propagation of findings or negative constraints.
Timestamp and source fields are weakly typed, while ingestion state, observability, verification execution, retention, retry, and quarantine behavior are absent.
Collections and strings have lower bounds but no upper resource bounds or processing limits.
Receipt v1 hard-codes finding-matrix v3 without declaring version negotiation or migration behavior.
JSON Schema supplies deterministic structural oracles, but semantic artifact integrity, exact role coverage, priority referential integrity, and enforceable negative constraints lack oracles.
Builders must choose identity formats, role cardinality, referential integrity, trust, state transitions, recovery, operational limits, propagation, and migration behavior.

Material unknowns remain around locator meaning, exact artifact-set completeness, finding-priority coverage, lineage semantics, ownership, consumers, trust, failure lifecycle, and GUI is explicitly outside this schema.
